data.description:
## Context / Problem

The sibling selector writes a labeled candidate manifest — per criterion, the candidates
with their direction, tier, supporting signals and rank. Nothing yet turns that into files
the eval runner can consume, and the file format is not free-form: `validate_eval_spec` under
`strict=True` rejects a spec that lacks an explicit `epochs`, a satisfiable `at_least(k)`
gate, a `coverage_threshold` in [0, 1], a non-empty `scorers` list holding at least one
registered deterministic scorer, a balanced dataset, or a non-empty `gold_set` whose entries
each carry an `input` and a `label` (`eval.py:252-272`, `eval.py:288-300`).

Two of those constraints cannot be satisfied by transcription alone. A criterion may yield
candidates on only one side of the fire/no-fire axis, which fails the balance rule at
`eval.py:252-255`; and a stale file from an earlier run would survive for a criterion that
has since become skipped, silently keeping a retired assertion in the suite.

## Approach

An emitter that reads the manifest and writes one `.eval.yaml` per criterion into a working
directory for the sibling admission runner. It issues no model call.

**Emitted spec fields.** Each file carries exactly the field set of the committed
`.rebar/evals/plan-review-project-portability.eval.yaml`: `prompt` (the criterion's prompt
id), `model`, `epochs: 3`, `gate: at_least(2)`, `coverage_threshold: 1.0`, a `scorers` list
holding the registered deterministic scorer `emits_valid_findings` from `eval_scorers`, a
`dataset` of `{id, corpus, criterion, expect}` cases, and a `gold_set` of `{input, label}`
entries. `epochs: 3` with `at_least(2)` matches the convention every shipped spec already
uses, so the emitted files need no second standard.

**Case selection.** At most 8 cases per criterion, at most 4 per side, taken in the manifest's
recorded rank order so the output is a deterministic function of the manifest.

**Balance guarantee.** A criterion that cannot supply at least one case on EACH side of the
axis, or no `gold_set`, emits NO file and is counted `skipped-unbalanced` in the emitter's
report. A one-sided dataset therefore never reaches the validator. The sibling self-healing
loop counts `skipped-unbalanced` as a failed attempt, so a persistently unbalanced criterion
is recorded by that child's `unreliable-criterion:` breaker rather than vanishing silently.

**Output lifecycle.** Each run writes a fresh temporary tree and atomically replaces the
working directory, so no file survives for a criterion that has become skipped or that
already has a spec.

## Scope

The emitter module under `src/rebar/llm/evals/`, its YAML serialization, the per-side case
selection, the balance refusal and the emitter report. It reads the manifest produced by the
sibling selector and writes only into its own working directory.

## Non-goals

- Deciding which candidates qualify, their tier, or their rank; the selector owns all of that
  and this child transcribes its recorded order.
- Writing into `.rebar/evals/` or admitting a spec; the admission runner owns both.
- Any model call.
- Emitting for a criterion that already has a spec, since `eval.py:69-78` resolves a project
  spec as a replacement and a mined file would delete the packaged cases.

## Testing

Unit tests over the serializer and the balance refusal using synthetic manifests, invoking
the real `validate_eval_spec(spec, strict=True)` on every emitted file rather than asserting
on YAML text. Every assertion is deterministic because no model is involved.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Every emitted spec returns zero errors from `validate_eval_spec(spec, strict=True)`;
      verified by `pytest` invoking the real validator over each emitted file.
- [ ] An emitted spec carries `epochs: 3`, `gate: at_least(2)`, `coverage_threshold: 1.0` and
      a `scorers` entry naming `emits_valid_findings`; verified by `pytest` asserting those
      four values on a spec built from a synthetic manifest.
- [ ] A criterion whose manifest holds candidates on only one side emits no file and is
      counted `skipped-unbalanced`; verified by `pytest` asserting the path is absent and the
      report names the criterion.
- [ ] A criterion whose manifest holds no `gold_set` material emits no file and is counted
      `skipped-unbalanced`; verified by `pytest` asserting the path is absent.
- [ ] Given a manifest with 6 ranked candidates on one side, the emitted dataset holds the
      first 4 in rank order; verified by `pytest` asserting the emitted case ids and order.
- [ ] A file written by a previous run for a criterion absent from the current manifest does
      not survive the next run; verified by `pytest` asserting the path is absent after the
      second run.
- [ ] Two consecutive runs over the same manifest emit byte-identical output; verified by
      `diff -r` of the two output trees exiting 0.
- [ ] The emitter completes with the repository's network guard active; verified by `pytest`
      running it under that guard.

## Definition of Done

`make lint`, `make typecheck` and `make test` pass; a run over the real manifest emits specs
that all pass the strict validator; the diff touches nothing under `.rebar/evals/` or
`src/rebar/llm/reviewers/`.

## Budget

**$0.** Emission is a pure function of the manifest.
data.title: Emit validated per-criterion eval specs from the labeled candidate manifest
